solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: the colon clause (lacked skull and most of tail) defines 'fragmentary' almost directly; 'duplicate' and 'living' are throwaway distractors nobody would pick, leaving only B (an antonym trap) as competition
S032-01.notes: Missing skull and tail = incomplete specimen -> fragmentary. 'intact' contradicts, 'duplicate' clashes with 'single', 'living' is absurd.

flags: minor: C 'outnumbered' does not fit grammatically/logically (a speech cannot outnumber people), so it is a throwaway distractor
S032-02.notes: Waverers moved to act and the bill passed -> speech roused them to action: galvanized. Alienated/bewildered are opposite in direction.

flags: minor: the key paraphrases the sentence's own 'Although the wall is extremely long, it is only...' structure, making it close to a lookup
S032-03.notes: Third sentence gives reasons (narrow, low color contrast) the wall is hard to see despite its length. A misreads 'extremely long' as the point; B unsupported; D wrong, the last sentence does not reject anything. Facts accurate (astronaut reports, few-meter width).

S032-04.notes: Ocean-type nitrogen in streamside leaves + bears carrying carcasses inland -> salmon deliver marine nutrients to forests. A overreaches (direct ocean water), C is about bears not trees, D reverses causation. Consistent with real marine-derived-nitrogen research (e.g., Reimchen; Helfield & Naiman on Sitka spruce growth).

flags: Answer cue: D is the only choice that mentions the 'gap' (the conclusion's key term) and it does the subtraction for the student, so no table reading is needed; also noticeably longer and unlike SAT style, which normally reports raw values for the student to compare. Consider stating the raw paired values (e.g., '45% vs. 38% ... 55% vs. 14%') instead of precomputed gaps.
minor: A is a plausible partial-support distractor (falling virtual share alone does not show the gap widens), which is good; B and C are weak
S032-05.notes: Gaps: 45-38=7, 52-31=21, 48-22=26, 55-14=41, strictly increasing; D numbers verified exact. C shows in-person > virtual everywhere but not widening; A ignores in-person (which is non-monotonic: 52 to 48).

S032-06.notes: Text 2: rise used on certain statements and works as a check inviting listener feedback, which directly counters the 'signals uncertainty' claim. B contradicts (directions are a sure context), C overgeneralizes 'mainly', D unsupported.

flags: minor: C is the only choice mentioning time ('17 hours'), so the goal keyword makes it an instant pick
S032-07.notes: Goal = how long they waited; only C cites the up-to-17-hour delay. Matches the real Kabadayi & Osvath 2017 Science study (ravens, up to 17 h).

S032-08.notes: No tailpipe emissions vs. battery manufacture emissions -> contrast/concession: 'Even so'. Therefore, Likewise, In other words all fail the contrast. Factual claims reasonable.

S032-09.notes: Introductory participle 'Excavated...' must modify the body: B. A makes investigators excavated; C 'there was' is a dangling/awkward subject and leaves a broken 'body, so well preserved' fragment; D makes the people excavated and repeats 'the people who found it'. Facts check: Tollund Man found in 1950 in a Danish bog near Silkeborg; finders thought it a recent murder and called police.

S032-10.notes: Two independent clauses joined by conjunctive adverb 'however' -> semicolon before, comma after: 'May; however, repairs...'. A is a comma splice (most common trap), B splice without comma, C lacks comma after 'however'.
